newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria completes first mass sell-off tender.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria completes first mass sell-off tender.

text.p: Bulgaria is due to end the first one-month mass sell-off auction of its mass privatisation programme on October 30 in line with its much-delayed reform plan, government officials said.

"With the end of the first auction session on Wednesday we have succesfully completed the first three stages of mass privatisation this year," head of the Mass Privatisation Centre Kalin Mitrev told a news conference.

Since January this year some three million Bulgarians or around 46 percent of the eligible population have bought voucher booklets each with a face value of 25,000 levs, which will enable them to take part in the privatisation of 1,050 firms.
Bulgarians can take part in the programme through privatisation funds or by directly swapping their vouchers for company shares at auctions. The auction sessions will continue through next year.
The three stages Mitrev referred to are registration, transfer of vouchers and auctions.
In the first auction session investors bid directly or through a dozen privatisation funds for shares in 968 state enterprises with total capital of 201.1 billion levs, said Mitrev.

The shares will be assigned according to bid price per share, first to the highest bidder, then to the second highest bidder and so on. Each enterprise has a minimum acceptable bid price based on its net asset value adjusted for overall supply and demand.

Bulgaria's Securities and Stock Exchange Commission (SSEC) has fully licensed so far some 60 privatisation funds of which 15 have foreign founders. The Bulgarian-Dutch privatisation fund, the third largest, was co-founded by ING bank and Bulgaria's Post Bank.
A post-privatisation fund is expected to be launched early next year jointly with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) aiming to offer equity loans to newly privatised firms.
"The EBRD is already screening some of the firms," said an EU PHARE programme official.
Under an agreement signed in April, the EBRD is expected to put up the venture fund's capital of up to 30 million Ecus, which will be used to buy minority stakes in newly privatised firms.
Trading of the enterprise and privatisation fund shares will begin six months afer the last auction session or by autumn of 1997, which is expected to boost the currently somnolent stock market.
